sermon.title: Historical Examples of Falling Away, Opposing God and His Church 04/15/2018
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: Pastor David G. Kincer gives historical examples of believers opposing what God was doing: crowds rejecting Jesus, the New Testament church and what it lacked, the falling away he dates to Constantine, and restoration movements from the 1300s through the Pentecostal outpouring, each opposed by the last. He ties the great awakenings to America’s founding and urges the church to ask for latter rain now.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added from the speaker’s pauses and then corrected by hand, and obvious caption errors (names, Bible references) were fixed; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: Garbled names (early reformers, a healing evangelist and others) are marked [unclear]. Kept as spoken: “2nd Thessalonians 1:7” for “Christ shall not come” (28:41); “Acts 3:20” for the restoration (34:32); Constantine made Christianity Rome’s religion in 325 AD (27:39); the 1840s Great Disappointment; the Pentecostal outpouring dated to the “early part of the nineteenth century” (40:26). Unverified: 90% of the American church believes Christ can come any minute (28:41); murderers serve five to seven years (47:13); Lutherans drowned Baptists (36:23). Sensitive content kept as spoken: in El Salvador, a family hunted down and butchered with machetes the bandits who killed a man, and “I said you did the right thing” (22:17–23:14). Clergy sexual immorality, babies buried in convents, priests as alcoholics (27:39–28:41). Suicides after the Great Disappointment. “Obama about destroyed our military”; liberals destroying the Constitution and the nation; welfare and food stamps (48:08–49:17, 55:43). Mormons in apostasy. Bob Jones University.
